# Development Rules

## Default Context

This repo contains multiple packages, but **`packages/coding-agent/`** is the primary focus. Unless otherwise specified, assume work refers to this package.

**Terminology**: When the architect says "agent" or asks "why is agent doing X", they mean the **coding-agent package implementation**, not you (the assistant). The coding-agent is a CLI tool — questions about its behavior refer to code in `packages/coding-agent/`, not your current session.

### Package Structure

| Package                 | Description                                                                             |
| ----------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `packages/ai`           | Multi-provider LLM client with streaming support                                        |
| `packages/catalog`      | Model catalog: bundled models.json, provider descriptors, model identity/classification |
| `packages/agent`        | Agent runtime with tool calling and state management                                    |
| `packages/coding-agent` | Main CLI application (primary focus)                                                    |
| `packages/tui`          | Terminal UI library with differential rendering                                         |
| `packages/natives`      | Bindings for native text/image/grep operations                                          |
| `packages/stats`        | Local observability dashboard (`tau stats`)                                             |
| `packages/tautype`      | ArkType-compatible schema validation with a lazy JIT runtime                            |
| `packages/utils`        | Shared utilities (logger, streams, temp files)                                          |
| `crates/tau-natives`     | Rust crate for performance-critical text/grep ops                                       |

**Catalog import convention**: code in this repo imports catalog _values_ (bundled models, model-thinking helpers, identity, descriptors, model manager/cache) from `@tau/tau-catalog/<module>` — never via `@tau/tau-ai`. The tau-ai barrel re-exports only the model/effort _types_ its own signatures use (`Model`, `Api`, `ThinkingConfig`, `Effort`, …); type-only imports of those from `@tau/tau-ai` are fine.

## GitHub

- Before posting a GitHub comment or creating an issue, MUST show the target and proposed text and obtain user confirmation. An explicit instruction to post supplied text to a specified target already counts as confirmation.
- A request to address or fix PR feedback permits drafting replies, not posting them without confirmation. A request only to get or check comments is read-only.
- When authorized to resolve review feedback, MUST verify the fix, obtain approval for a factual reply citing the change and verification, and post it in the existing thread before resolving. NEVER resolve if the reply is unapproved or posting fails.
- Permission to work on a PR does not authorize unrelated comments or issue creation.

### Pull requests

When authorized to create or edit a contributor-submitted PR, follow the checklist below. RoboOMP-managed PRs follow their dedicated workflow and enforced body format in `python/robtau/src/prompts/system_append.md` instead.

- MUST read `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md` first. Preserve the template sections and checklist, including when shortening an existing description.
- MUST obtain at least one sentence written by the contributor in their own words explaining what changed and why, as required by `CONTRIBUTING.md`. If it is missing, ask the contributor; NEVER generate a substitute. Preserve that sentence during edits.
- For user-facing changes, MUST follow the [Changelog](#changelog) attribution rules. Internal issue fixes keep their issue links. For external contributions, add the PR link and contributor credit after GitHub assigns the number, then push the entry before marking the changelog checklist item complete.
- MUST read back the published PR description after creating or editing it. Check only verified checklist items; explain skipped or inapplicable checks in `Testing`.

## Code Quality

- No `any` unless absolutely necessary.
- **NEVER use `ReturnType<>`** — use the actual type name.
- **NEVER use inline imports** — no `await import()`, no `import("pkg").Type` in type positions, no dynamic type imports. Always top-level.
- Check `node_modules` for external API types instead of guessing.
- **Barrel exports**: prefer `export * from "./module"` over named re-exports, including `export type { ... } from`. In pure `index.ts` barrels, use star re-exports even for single-specifier cases. If stars create ambiguity, remove the redundant export path; do not keep duplicates.
- **Class privacy**: use ES `#private` fields; leave externally accessible members bare. **No `private`/`protected`/`public` keyword on fields or methods**, except on **constructor parameter properties** where TypeScript requires it (e.g. `constructor(private readonly session: ToolSession)`).
- **Promises**: use `Promise.withResolvers()` instead of `new Promise((resolve, reject) => ...)`.
- **Prompts**: never build prompts in code (no inline strings, template literals, or concatenation). Prompts live in static `.md` files; use Handlebars for dynamic content. Import them via `import content from "./prompt.md" with { type: "text" }` — not `readFile`.
- **Worker scripts**: workers re-enter the CLI entrypoint; never spawn separate worker entry modules. `cli.ts` declares itself as the worker host at startup (`declareWorkerHostEntry()` from `@tau/tau-utils/env`) and dispatches hidden argv selectors (`__tau_worker_stats_sync`, `__tau_worker_tab`, `__tau_worker_js_eval`, `__tau_worker_tiny_inference`) before loading the command registry. Spawn sites use:
  ```ts
  import { workerHostEntry } from "@tau/tau-utils";
  const hostEntry = workerHostEntry();
  const worker = hostEntry
  	? new Worker(hostEntry, { type: "module", argv: ["__tau_worker_<name>"] })
  	: new Worker(new URL("./<worker>.ts", import.meta.url).href, { type: "module" });
  ```
  When the process was started from the tau CLI — source `cli.ts`, npm-bundle `dist/cli.js`, or compiled binary — `workerHostEntry()` is `Bun.main` and the worker re-enters the single entry module, so no per-worker `--compile` entrypoints or bundle entries exist. Outside a CLI host (`bun test`, SDK embedding, standalone `tau-stats`) it returns `null` and the direct-module fallback loads the worker source. New worker kinds MUST add their selector to the dispatch table in `cli.ts` and keep the fallback branch.
  History: `with { type: "file" }` only copied the entry as a raw asset (workers crashed silently in compiled binaries — issues #1011, #1027), and the later literal-path + extra-entrypoint pattern required keeping spawn literals and two build scripts in sync (issue #1150). The smoke probe below is the live validation of this contract.
  Validate any new worker with the dedicated smoke probe: `tau --smoke-test` spawns the stats sync worker and the tiny-model subprocess, pings them, and exits — it's wired into `ci:test:smoke` and `scripts/install-tests/run-ci.sh` so binary, source-link, and tarball installs all exercise it. Add a sibling smoke if the new worker is on a different module graph.

## Central Utilities

Before writing a helper, check whether one already exists — `packages/coding-agent/src/utils/`, `@tau/tau-utils`, `@tau/tau-tui`, and the domain modules next to your callsite. This applies to **everything**: VCS wrappers, formatting/truncation/path-display helpers, image handling, clipboard, streams, temp files, caching. The central versions carry hardening a fresh copy always loses (timeouts, output caps, non-interactive env, lock avoidance, caching, TUI sanitization).

- Search first: `grep` for the operation before implementing it. Two implementations of the same thing is a bug even when both work.
- Examples of the pattern: `@tau/tau-natives/vcs` and `src/utils/active-repo-context.ts` are the only sanctioned way to run git/jj (`import * as vcs from "@tau/tau-natives/vcs"` — never hand-spawn via `$`/`Bun.spawn`); rendering goes through the helpers in TUI Sanitization below (`replaceTabs`, `truncateToWidth`, `shortenPath`, `PREVIEW_LIMITS`) rather than ad-hoc string math.
- Missing capability? Extend the central helper (new option, new sub-function on the namespace) and call it — don't fork its logic locally.

## Bun Over Node

Use Bun APIs where they provide a cleaner alternative; fall back to `node:*` only for what Bun doesn't cover. **Never spawn shell commands for operations with proper APIs** (e.g., don't `Bun.spawnSync(["mkdir", "-p", dir])` — use `mkdirSync`).

### Quick reference

| Operation       | Use                                       | Not                                |
| --------------- | ----------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| File read/write | `Bun.file()`, `Bun.write()`               | `readFileSync`, `writeFileSync`    |
| Spawn process   | `` $`cmd` ``, `Bun.spawn()`               | `child_process`                    |
| Sleep           | `Bun.sleep(ms)`                           | `setTimeout` promise               |
| Binary lookup   | `$which("git")` from `@tau/tau-utils` | `spawnSync(["which", "git"])`      |
| HTTP server     | `Bun.serve()`                             | `http.createServer()`              |
| SQLite          | `bun:sqlite`                              | `better-sqlite3`                   |
| Hashing         | `Bun.hash()`, `Bun.password.*`, WebCrypto | `node:crypto`                      |
| Path resolution | `import.meta.dir`, `import.meta.path`     | `fileURLToPath` dance              |
| JSON5           | `Bun.JSON5.parse()` / `.stringify()`      | `json5` package                    |
| JSONL           | `Bun.JSONL.parse()` / `.parseChunk()`     | `text.split("\n").map(JSON.parse)` |
| String width    | `Bun.stringWidth()`                       | `get-east-asian-width`, custom     |
| Text wrapping   | `Bun.wrapAnsi()`                          | custom ANSI-aware wrappers         |

### Process execution

Prefer Bun Shell (`` $`cmd` ``) for simple commands:

```typescript
import { $ } from "bun";

const result = await $`git status`.cwd(dir).quiet().nothrow();
if (result.exitCode === 0) {
	const text = result.text();
}

$`do-stuff ${tmpFile}`.quiet().nothrow(); // fire and forget
```

Methods: `.quiet()`, `.nothrow()`, `.text()`, `.cwd(path)`.

Use `Bun.spawn`/`Bun.spawnSync` only for: long-running processes (LSP, kernels), streaming stdin/stdout/stderr (SSE, JSON-RPC), or process control (signals, kill, complex lifecycle).

When using `pipe` mode, cast the stream:

```typescript
const child = Bun.spawn(["cmd"], { stdout: "pipe", stderr: "pipe" });
const reader = (child.stdout as ReadableStream<Uint8Array>).getReader();
```

### Node module imports

Always use **namespace imports** for `node:fs`, `node:path`, `node:os`:

```typescript
import * as fs from "node:fs/promises";
import * as path from "node:path";
import * as os from "node:os";
```

- Async-only file → `node:fs/promises`.
- Needs both sync and async → `node:fs`, then `fs.promises.xxx` for async.

### File I/O

Prefer Bun:

```typescript
const text = await Bun.file(path).text();
const data = await Bun.file(path).json();
await Bun.write(path, data); // auto-creates parent dirs
```

Use `node:fs/promises` for directory ops (`fs.mkdir`, `fs.rm`, `fs.readdir`) — Bun has no native directory APIs. Avoid sync APIs in async flows; use sync only when forced by a synchronous interface.

**Anti-patterns:**

- `existsSync`/`readFileSync`/`writeFileSync` in async code → `Bun.file()` APIs.
- `mkdir(dirname(path), …)` before `Bun.write(path, …)` → redundant; `Bun.write` handles it.
- `if (await file.exists()) { await file.json() }` → two syscalls plus race. Use try-catch with `isEnoent`:
  ```typescript
  import { isEnoent } from "@tau/tau-utils";
  try {
  	return await Bun.file(path).json();
  } catch (err) {
  	if (isEnoent(err)) return null;
  	throw err;
  }
  ```
- Multiple `Bun.file(path)` handles for the same path (including across `checkX`/`loadX` helpers).
- `Buffer.from(await Bun.file(x).arrayBuffer())` → `await fs.readFile(path)`.
- Existence check + try-catch around the same read → drop the existence check.

### Streams

Prefer centralized helpers:

```typescript
import { readStream, readLines } from "./utils/stream";
const text = await readStream(child.stdout);
for await (const line of readLines(stream)) {
	/* ... */
}
```

Manual reader loops only when the protocol requires it (SSE, streaming JSON-RPC).

### Misc

- **Sleep**: `await Bun.sleep(ms)`, never `new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, ms))`.
- **Password hashing**: `Bun.password.hash(pw, "bcrypt")` / `Bun.password.verify(pw, hash)`.
- **String width**: `Bun.stringWidth(text, { countAnsiEscapeCodes?: false })`.
- **Wrapping**: `Bun.wrapAnsi(text, width, { wordWrap, hard, trim })`.

## Model/Provider Policy Lives in KDL

**NEVER hard-code model- or provider-conditional policy in TypeScript.** No `id.includes("claude")`, no model-name regexes, no per-model lookup tables (effort ladders, pricing, context windows, modalities, API routing, quirk flags). All of it belongs in the KDL rule tree at `packages/catalog/src/compat/rules/`, compiled by `bun run gen:compat` into the committed `rules.json` and resolved at build time via `resolveModelPolicy`/`buildModel`.

Ownership strata (see `src/compat/rules/README.md`):

- `taxonomy/*.kdl` — identity: class membership, families, revision extraction, reviewed overrides, suffix collapse.
- `classes/*.kdl` — model-lineage truths (behavior inherent to a model line, on any host).
- `providers/*.kdl` — deployment contracts (behavior a host imposes), plus documented exact-id residue.
- `runtime/behavior.kdl` — heuristics that run before/outside exact model lookup (`api-routes`, `model-limits`, `exclude-models`, `pricing-peer`, hosted defaults).

Rules for TS code:

- Branching on model identity in TS is allowed **only** through structured facts from `classifyModel()` (`class`/`family`/`revision`/effort facts) — never through string matching on ids, and prefer a KDL axis when one can express the policy.
- Discovery mappers map authoritative upstream fields as reported; seed neutral values only for fields the upstream omits or misreports **and** KDL explicitly owns via a correction axis (`input-modalities`, `cost-patch`, `limits-patch`, `context-window-floor`, thinking axes). Assert rule-owned corrections through `buildModel`; raw discovery specs remain the right assertion surface for parsing/normalization contracts.
- An id that no selector can isolate gets an exact-id `models` residue rule with a comment — never a special case in TS.
- Equal-rank rule overlaps throw `AmbiguousOverlapError` at resolve time; fix with an explicit `priority=` in KDL, not code.
- After editing rules: `bun run gen:compat` and commit `rules.json` alongside the `.kdl` change.

## Generated Files

**NEVER edit `packages/catalog/src/models.json` directly.** It is generated from upstream sources (stencil.so, provider catalog discovery, OpenCode docs) by `packages/catalog/scripts/generate-models.ts` and the descriptors/resolvers in `packages/catalog/src/provider-models/`. Hand-edits get overwritten on the next regen. The same applies to `packages/catalog/src/compat/rules.json`, compiled from the KDL tree by `bun run gen:compat`.

To change an entry, fix the source:

- **Model/provider policy** (identity, thinking ladders, wire quirks, modality/limit/pricing corrections, API routing, roster exclusions) → the KDL tree in `packages/catalog/src/compat/rules/` (see the section above).
- **Provider catalog entries** (default model, discovery factory/flags) → the `CATALOG_PROVIDERS` table in `packages/catalog/src/provider-models/descriptors.ts`.
- **Discovery/request plumbing** (endpoint shapes, auth, response parsing) → the mappers in `packages/catalog/src/provider-models/openai-compat.ts`.
- **Generator wiring** (upstream merges, premium multipliers, post-processing order) → `packages/catalog/scripts/generate-models.ts`.

Regenerate with `bun run gen:compat` and/or `bun run gen:models` and commit the generated files alongside the source change. Add a regression test against the **rule/descriptor/mapper**, not the bundled JSON, so it survives upstream metadata shifts.

## Logging and CLI Output

Code that may run while the TUI, RPC, SDK, workers, or background runtimes are active MUST NOT use `console.log`/`error`/`warn`; it corrupts rendering or protocols. Use the centralized logger:

```typescript
import { logger } from "@tau/tau-utils";

logger.error("MCP request failed", { url, method });
logger.warn("Theme file invalid, using fallback", { path });
logger.debug("LSP fallback triggered", { reason });
```

Logs go to `~/.tau/logs/tau.YYYY-MM-DD.log` with automatic rotation. Standalone CLI commands that exit without entering the TUI MAY use `console.*` or process streams for intentional user-facing output. Keep structured stdout clean. This exception is semantic, not filename-based; shared code must use `logger` or an explicit output sink.

## TUI Sanitization

All text displayed in tool renderers must be sanitized. Raw content (file contents, error messages, tool output) breaks terminal rendering: tabs → visual holes, long lines → overflow, paths → leak home directory.

**Rules:**

- **Tabs → spaces** via `replaceTabs()` (from `@tau/tau-tui` or `../tools/render-utils`).
- **Truncate** lines with `truncateToWidth()` / `ui.truncate()`. Use `TRUNCATE_LENGTHS` constants.
- **Shorten paths** with `shortenPath()` (replaces home with `~`).
- **Preview limits** from `PREVIEW_LIMITS`. No ad-hoc numbers.

**Apply to every render path**, not just the happy one:

- Success output (file previews, command output, search results).
- **Error messages** — these often embed file content (e.g., patch failure messages include unmatched lines). If a message contains file content, it needs `replaceTabs()`.
- Diff content (added and removed).
- Streaming previews.

### Streaming tool previews

Tool-call previews can have **multiple render paths**. If you add preview-only fields or depend on partially streamed args, update every path — not only the final renderer. Streamed argument buffers decode into display args via `decodeStreamedToolArgs` / `ToolArgsRevealController` (`modes/controllers/tool-args-reveal.ts`); both the live event path and transcript rebuilds must go through them — never spread provider-parsed `arguments` next to a raw `__partialJson` (parsed args lag the stream by a throttled parse window).

For the bash tool specifically:

- The pending preview may need raw `partialJson`, not just parsed `arguments`. Parsed args lag until a JSON object closes, which makes inline env assignments appear only at the end.
- Preserve preview-only fields (e.g. `__partialJson`) through `event-controller.ts`, transcript rebuilds in `ui-helpers.ts`, and merged call/result rendering in `tool-execution.ts`. Missing one path causes inconsistent previews.
- `ToolExecutionComponent.#buildRenderContext()` for bash must work even before a result exists — the renderer uses call args plus render context to show the command preview while streaming.
- Verify both live streaming and rebuilt transcript paths after any bash preview change. A fix in one path does not fix the other.

## Commands

- NEVER commit unless asked.
- Never use `tsc`/`npx tsc` — always `bun check`.
- Never run `cargo test` directly for Rust tests — use `bun run test:rs`. It runs `cargo nextest run` (config: `.config/nextest.toml`) followed by a `cargo test --doc` pass, because nextest does not execute doctests. The doctest pass currently executes nothing (tau-natives is a `cdylib`, which rustdoc skips; tau-builtins' examples are `ignore`d vendored uutils docs) and exists so the first runnable doctest added to a lib crate is actually run.
- Merge commits (maintainer merges of PRs) follow: `Merge PR #<number>: <conventional PR subject> (@<author>)` — e.g. `Merge PR #6386: feat(catalog): add native Meta Model API provider (@eggpeat)`.
## Rust Build Profiles

Profiles live in the root `Cargo.toml`; `.cargo/config.toml` carries the settings Cargo.toml cannot express. Both are committed, so no local `~/.cargo/config.toml` is required.

| Profile | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `dev` | Default. Line tables for our crates, no debuginfo for deps, deps at `opt-level = 2`. |
| `release` | Shipping build: fat LTO, 1 codegen unit, stripped. |
| `local` | Fast local release iteration: thin LTO, 16 codegen units, incremental. |
| `profiling` | `release` codegen with symbols kept, for `perf`/`samply`/Instruments. |
| `ci` | Thin LTO, no debuginfo, stripped. |

**Never set `split-debuginfo = "off"` on a profile that has debuginfo.** On Mach-O the linker never merges DWARF into the executable — it writes a debug map (`N_OSO`) pointing at the `.o` files, and `"unpacked"` is what keeps those files. With `"off"` every backtrace frame in our own crates silently loses `file:line`; the `panicked at foo.rs:3` header still prints (that is `#[track_caller]`, not debuginfo), which makes the loss easy to miss. `ci` may use `"off"` only because it sets `debug = false`.

`embed-metadata = false` (in `.cargo/config.toml`) keeps crate metadata in `.rmeta` instead of duplicating it into every rlib — measured 196 MB → 130 MB on a reqwest-sized graph at identical build times. Its accepted spelling is toolchain-coupled; keep it in sync with `rust-toolchain.toml`.

Rejected, with measurements, so nobody re-litigates them: **sccache** (cannot cache incremental, bin, or proc-macro crates — measured slower than not using it), **mold** (ELF-only; no Mach-O support), and **`panic = "abort"` on `dev`** (Cargo ignores `panic` for the test profile, so the whole dep graph builds twice — 131 MB → 214 MB).

## Testing Guidance

Test the contract the system exposes — not the easiest internal detail to assert.

- Every new test must defend one **concrete, externally observable contract**: behavior, output shape, state transition, error mapping, or a regression-prone parsing boundary. If you cannot name the contract, do not add the test.

### Good vs. bad test filter

- **Name the failure mode.** Every test MUST state what a consumer observes if it regresses. Cannot name one? NEVER add it.
- **Good: transformation.** One fixture MAY prove parse/render/normalize/encode/resolve behavior when output is computed, not echoed.
- **Good: branch or boundary.** Distinct inputs, empty values, malformed input, version/provider routing, and state transitions MUST prove distinct outcomes.
- **Good: external contract.** Exact bytes/shape MAY be asserted when a provider, parser, protocol, or persisted consumer reads them.
- **Good: precedence or negative contract.** Keep explicit `false`/override-wins assertions and required absence only when they prevent a documented leak, downgrade, 400, or incompatible wire field.
- **Good: regression.** A repro MUST trigger the prior real failure path and assert the corrected observable result.
- **Bad: static echo.** NEVER test a constructor/builder merely copied a fixture or baked constant into an in-memory config/metadata field.
- **Bad: success passthrough.** NEVER assert `fn(x) === x` when `x` was already supplied/declared valid; assert a transform, rejection, or downstream effect instead.
- **Bad: wording/defaults.** NEVER assert prompt/UI boilerplate, a default literal, object existence, non-empty output, or length growth without a consumer contract.
- **Bad: duplicate rows.** Parameterized/loop rows MUST each cover a distinct branch, provider/model path, or consumer contract; delete same-path duplicates.
- **Metadata exception.** Exact metadata, identity, ordering, or `undefined` MAY remain only when a downstream consumer depends on it and the test establishes branch, precedence, negative-contract, wire, or regression evidence.
- **Termination exception.** For cyclic/large inputs, assert a bounded output, surfaced error, or state change; bare `not.toThrow()` is insufficient.
- No placeholder tests, tautologies, or "the code ran" assertions (`expect(true).toBe(true)`, bare `not.toThrow()`, non-empty string checks, length-grew checks, "prompt exists" checks without semantic assertion).
- Prefer contract-level tests over implementation details. Avoid asserting internal helper wiring, field assignment, singleton identity, incidental ordering, prompt boilerplate, or passthrough option forwarding unless another component depends on that exact detail.
- Don't duplicate coverage across abstraction levels. If an integration test already proves the behavior, drop the narrower unit test that restates it through mocks.
- Tests **must be full-suite safe**, not just file-local safe. No long-lived file-wide mutations of `Bun.*`, `process.platform`, `process.env`, or `Bun.env` when a narrower seam exists. Prefer per-test `vi.spyOn(...)` with `vi.restoreAllMocks()` in `afterEach`. A test that passes alone but poisons later files is broken.
- **Never use `mock.module()`**. Bun's `mock.module()` mutates the global module registry and leaks across files ([oven-sh/bun#12823](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/issues/12823)). Use `spyOn` on the imported module object instead. For pass deps, import the pass and spy on `.run`. For package deps, namespace-import and spy on the exported function.
- For lifecycle/stateful code, prefer one test per invariant or transition over several tiny tests asserting one field each from the same transition.
- For error handling, trigger the real failure path and assert the surfaced contract — don't instantiate error classes directly or inspect internal metadata.
- Smoke tests are acceptable only when they catch a failure mode narrower tests would miss. "Package boots" or "command starts" alone is not enough.
- Assert exact strings, ordering, and formatting only when downstream code parses or depends on the exact bytes. Otherwise assert semantic content.
- Compile-time guarantees → type checks/type tests, not runtime placeholders.
- **Never source-grep.** A test that reads an implementation file (`.ts`/`.rs`/build script) and asserts on its _text_ — `expect(src).toContain("someCall()")`, `.toMatch(/import .../)`, `.not.toContain("oldName")`, or "comment must say X" — is banned. It tests how code _looks_, not what it _does_: it breaks on harmless refactors (comment reflow, rename, import reorder) and passes while the behavior is broken. Assert the observable contract instead (run the code, check output/state/error), use the runtime smoke probe for wiring you cannot exercise in-process, and enforce structural invariants (no value-import of X, no self-import) with a type test or an oxlint rule — never a string scan of the source. (Reading a file your code _wrote_ — apply-patch result, generated bundle, temp fixture — and asserting on that output is fine; that is behavior, not a source grep.)
- Don't add tests for tiny low-risk changes unless they protect a real contract or fix a regression-prone edge case.
- Prefer focused package-local verification for the changed area.

## Changelog

Location: `packages/*/CHANGELOG.md` (per package).

**NEVER update changelogs unless explicitly asked.** Do not add, edit, or reorder entries as part of a feature, fix, or PR unless the architect requests it.

**Format** — sections under `## [Unreleased]`:

- `### Breaking Changes` (first if present)
- `### Added`
- `### Changed`
- `### Fixed`
- `### Removed`

**Rules:**

- New entries always go under `## [Unreleased]`.
- Entries are one line, brief, and user-facing: lead with what the architect will see or can now do. Root-cause narration and implementation detail belong in the commit/PR, not the changelog.
- Never modify already-released sections (e.g., `## [0.12.2]`) — they are immutable.
- Don't flag changelog section order or formatting in reviews or PRs — `bun run release` runs `fix-changelogs` which normalizes everything automatically.

**Attribution:**

- Internal (from issues): `Fixed foo bar ([#123](https://github.com/toxicwind/tau/issues/123))`.
- External contributions: `Added feature X ([#456](https://github.com/toxicwind/tau/pull/456) by [@username](https://github.com/username))`.

## Releasing

1. Ensure all changes since last release are in each affected package's `[Unreleased]` section.
2. Run `bun run release`.

The script handles version bump, CHANGELOG finalization, commit, tag, publish, and adding new `[Unreleased]` sections.

## Non-negotiable (verbatim, applies to every agent on this box)

1. **MAXIMAL.** Go fully, or don't go. Fix-repairs, never report-only audits.
   No review gates: commit, push, forward-only.
2. **The box is live.** 89+ pitchfork+mise daemons. Additive only — never remove or

## The vibe meta-todo (first-class, resets every task)

Every `todowrite` list ENDS with a final **vibe meta-todo** (always last, always
the reset). It holds the estate's whole doctrine so even mid-task you never lose
the thread:

- **Free-will / MAXIMAL / first-class / future-usable / cutting-edge.** Never
  "report-only" — always _fix-forward_. If something is slow, blocked, or basic,
  that's a signal to race the fastest available path, not to stop.
- **Race faster with borrow + papers, DURING the task, not just at planning:**
  on any slow/blocked step route `ast-grep` → `bm25` → **paper-finder** →
  **forge borrow** → `background_process`, in that order, before ANY workaround.
  Never retry the same slow command; a breach without a raced fix is a defect.
- **After research, spawn the next 6 complex todos** capturing the cutting-edge
  directions found and execute them in sequence — don't let the research
  evaporate.
- **2s breach = opportunity, not failure.** Every breach is the trigger to find
  the faster pattern or paper, via the AST tools.
- **Verbosity stays ON.** This project's ethos is MAXIMAL: go fully or don't go.
- **Additive-only** on the live box (never remove/disable a peer/daemon/model
  without explicit order). **Secrets never committed.** **One writer per
  subtree.** **Everything pushed** (commit/push/forward-only).
- **End every task** by re-visiting this vibe todo as the reset — it is the
  standing meta-context for the whole estate.

## Tooling — MCP-first doctrine

### Gatehouse MCP: First-Class Over Raw Bash

Calling raw bash subshells or binaries is flawed when **Gatehouse MCP**
(`http://127.0.0.1:25127/mcp`) and first-class retrieve tools exist. Gatehouse
federates MCP tools across the box — FFS, BM25, memory (`recall`/`retain`/`reflect`),
browser-keeper CDP (`computer` / `:9223`), and more — behind a unified interface.

**Use native tool calls and Gatehouse MCP interfaces over raw terminal commands.**
The following first-class tools are the primary interface, not bash:

| Tool         | Purpose                                                       |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `read`       | File/URL/document reading with outline, budget, selectors     |
| `bash`       | Real facts/pipelines only — not specialized-tool work         |
| `edit`       | Anchored patch edits                                          |
| `write`      | Create/overwrite files                                        |
| `eval`       | Python/IPython, browser, computer control                     |
| `glob`       | File/directory discovery                                      |
| `find`       | Behavior-to-source mapping (first for unknown locations)      |
| `web_search` | Structured web search                                         |
| `lsp`        | Symbol-aware code intelligence (navigation, refactor, rename) |

#### Gatehouse MCP federated tools

Gatehouse at `http://127.0.0.1:25127/mcp` exposes MCP resources and tools for:

- **FFS** (full-text search, BM25 ranking, symbol indexing)
- **BM25** (relevance-ranked text search across the estate)
- **Memory** (`recall`, `retain`, `reflect` — long-term memory queries)
- **Browser-keeper CDP** (`:9223` — Chromium DevTools Protocol, `computer` object)
- **GitHub** (`gh` wrapper for repos, PRs, search, checkout, push)
- **Debug** (`xd://debug` — debugger access, breakpoints, stepping)
- **Ast-grep** (`xd://ast_grep`, `xd://ast_edit` — AST-aware search and rewrite)
- **Session tools** (`xd://retain`, `xd://recall`, `xd://reflect`, `xd://hashline`)

**Rule:** When a first-class tool or Gatehouse MCP tool exists for a task, use it.
Raw bash is a last resort — acceptable only for system introspection that no MCP tool
covers (e.g. `docker ps`, `ss`, `curl` for health checks).

### FFS — The Universal Search/Read Interface

`ffs` is a single CLI over a persistent on-disk index (Bigram, Bloom, Symbol, Outline).

| When you need to…                    | Use `ffs …`           | Notes                                                   |
| ------------------------------------ | --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| Find a file by name fragment         | `find <needle>`       | substring, case-insensitive; `--scored` adds role/socle |
| Match by shape/glob                  | `glob '**/<pattern>'` | shell glob (`**`,`*`,`?`,`[…]`)                         |
| Content match, one pattern           | `grep <regex>`        | ripgrep semantics; `--group` groups by enclosing symbol |
| Content match, many needles          | `multi-grep`          | Aho-Corasick literal AND/OR                             |
| Read a file without flooding context | `read <path>`         | §budget-aware _outline_ by default; `--full` raw        |
| Sketch a single file's structure     | `outline <path>`      | tree-sitter, `--style agent/…`                          |
| Resolve a symbol to its definition   | `symbol <name>`       | tree-sitter AST, not substring                          |
| Who refers to this symbol            | `callers <name>`      | `--hops N` BFS (≤5)                                     |
| What this symbol calls               | `callees <name>`      | `--depth N`                                             |
| Defs + usages in one shot            | `refs <name>`         | full defs + paged callers                               |
| Full card per definition             | `flow <name>`         | def+signature+body+callees+callers                      |
| Peers at same scope                  | `siblings <name>`     | same class/file/module                                  |
| Imports + dependents of a file       | `deps <path>`         | import graph of a file                                  |
| Rank blast radius of a change        | `impact <symbol>`     | score = direct×3 + imports×2 + transitive×1             |
| See the whole workspace              | `map` / `overview`    | file counts + token estimates                           |
| Warm the indexes                     | `index`               | build Bigram/Bloom/Symbol/Outline caches                |
| Be an MCP server                     | `mcp`                 | replaces Grep/Glob/Read for agents                      |
| Recall the guide                     | `guide`               | print the embedded doc                                  |

- **Global flags**: `--root <dir>`, `--format text|json`. Listing commands
  (`find/symbol/callers/callees/refs/flow/siblings`) page with
  `--limit N --offset N`. Use `--limit` aggressively (5–20 usually enough).
- **Index-aware**: search correctness depends on fresh indexes. If a search
  returns nothing that should exist, `ffs index` then retry.
- **Symbols**: trailing `*` = prefix glob (`symbol Foo*`).
- Never `fd`/`rg`/`find`/`grep`/`cat` — that is a doctrine violation, not a
  fallback. `bash -lc` read-only is acceptable only when ffs cannot express the
  query (e.g. `docker ps`, `ss`, `curl`).

- **Patch safely with hashline**: ALWAYS carry the `read` anchor
  (`SWAP 641:3f2a..674:9b1c:`); never mix a bare op after a line-count-changing
  op; re-read every file and diff the `~/-/+` lines after every patch.
- **Live token counting**: `tok` (see `tok --help`).
- **The 2-second rule (MANDATORY): `run-fast` wraps EVERY command.**
  `/home/toxic/estate/bin/run-fast <cmd…>` — hard 2.0s wall-clock per
  execution; streams output live; deadline breach = FAILED, and the breach
  is the trigger to race a FASTER alternative (better code, new libs,
  pattern-borrow) — never to wait longer. Inherently long work (network
  fetches, builds, installs) goes to `background_process` or a pitchfork
  daemon — never a blocking tool call. The bash tool auto-shims known-slow
  commands through run-fast (`bin/bash-2s-shim.sh`, sourced in the shell).
- **Verification**: parallelize reads; persist every check's FULL output to a file
  and give a PASS/FAIL per check with evidence. Truncated stdio is a defect, not
  a result. Two real failures on one target → stop and replan.

## Provider doctrine

- **Provider catalog SSOT — Pinax**: `@toxicwind/pinax` (`estate/ranch/pinax`) is
  the single source of truth. It generates `tau-models.yml`, `kappa-models.json`,
  `providers.go`, `providers.rs`, and `providers.json`. **"roost" is retired and
  purged** — never reference it.
- **Primary fast inference — FreeInference** (`freeinference.org/v1`):
  models: `qwen3.6-35b`, `glm-5.3-flash`, `deepseek-v4-flash`, `minimax-m3`.
  **No hard provider concurrency cap** (proven 2026-10-22: 4 concurrent → all 200,
  no 429/rate-limit headers; Pinax defines no cap). A "429 with retry-after:1" seen
  from proxied tool calls is a **local Gatehouse/limiter concurrency shed**, not the
  provider. When a provider opts into client `unlimitedRetryOn429` (default off),
  ride a concurrency-contained 429 through (retry) rather than hard-stopping. The
  `maxConcurrency: 2` number is a **Kappa client knob** (`kappa.jsonc`), not provider
  doctrine. See `estate/ranch/estate-recon/muse-meta-hatch/docs/field-notes/kite-fleet-recon/
FIX-usage-limit-as-dev-env.md`.
- **Orchestration: Corral + DelendAI**:
  Multi-agent fleet orchestration is **Corral** (`@estate/corral`, `estate/ranch/corral`)
  merged with **DelendAI** (`shared-checkout-merge` development profile, proposal
  guardian, and speculative merge queue). **"super-ralph" is retired.**
- **DelendAI Checkpoint Fast-Path — `delend-quick`**:
  Under `shared-checkout-merge` repositories (such as `ranch`), direct commits to
  `main` are strictly blocked by the reference-transaction guard. Use the universal
  first-class helper `/home/toxic/estate/bin/delend-quick -m "<message>"` (on PATH).
  It auto-discovers changed paths, climbs to the repository root, safely normalizes
  the work-ref namespace (`heads/wip/${agent}/implement/${proposal}-${slice}-g1/${topic}`),
  executes `delendai work checkpoint`, and pushes the work-ref to `origin`.

## 25xxx fleet & dashboards

- **89 active supervised daemons** on 25xxx managed by pitchfork.
- **ranch-ui (port 25218)**: Consolidated dashboard serving DelendAI control plane
  SPA + herd proxy.
- **range-ui (port 25156)**: Vite dev server with `/api` proxying to control-api on

## Working rules

- **Docker is scoped, not banned (decided 2026-10-16).** Two lanes:
  - **Lane A — estate services** (MCP servers, routers, daemons, watchdogs): native,
    supervised by pitchfork+mise. **Docker forbidden** — a container duplicating a
    pitchfork daemon steals its ports and strands stale NAT rules (rustdesk outage
    2026-10-16: stale REDIRECT rules broke remote 25221/25222 for days).
  - **Lane B — ops/websites deployables** (effusion-labs, arlockworks stacks): docker
    compose, in the site's own repo/infra dir, ports pinned in `config/ports.env`,
    bound to 127.0.0.1/tailnet unless intentionally public.
  - **Tie-breaker: one supervisor per service.** Before adding a pitchfork daemon,
    check `docker ps -a`; before dockerizing, check pitchfork. Compose file lives
    in the repo that owns the site.

- Stage scratch under `/home/toxic/`, unique per-task dirs (`mktemp -d`), never
  `rm -rf` a shared hardcoded /tmp path. Never leave a backgrounded bridge call
  outstanding — wait for delivery.
- One writer per subtree; many readers. Race redundant read-only approaches;
  first valid answer wins. Gates serialize: token scrub → pushes; stash merge →
  build.
- Luis guesses are starting points, not specs — fuzz/verify, don't anchor.

## Scope split (nested AGENTS.md)

| Path                                   | Owner of these rules                                      |
| -------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `/home/toxic/estate/AGENTS.md`         | estate control-plane: repos, skills, grasp-hub, pitchfork |
| `/home/toxic/estate/ranch/*/AGENTS.md` | each ranch component repo's own contract                  |

**Container path**: `$HOME/AGENTS.md` = this file; `$HOME/estate/AGENTS.md` = the
estate mirror. Every nested file declares _what it refines and where_; none
repeats or contradicts the universal contract above.

## Agent customizations + skills hub (2026-10-16)

- **Skills hub = grasp-hub** (`/home/toxic/estate/grasp-hub`; supersedes the old
  skills-hub MCP naming). Register a new skill by dropping it in
  `/home/toxic/estate/skills/<name>/` (SKILL.md frontmatter required), symlinking
  into `grasp-hub/skills/<cluster>/<name>`, then proving pickup:
  `node bin/grasp-hub.js list | grep <name>` and `node bin/grasp-hub.js validate`
  must be green. The MCP server (`grasp-hub/mcp/server.ts`) wraps this CLI.
- **Guide convention is REQUIRED** for every `*-guide` project: flat R-NNN rule
  ids (renumbering forbidden; commits cite ids), a Why paragraph naming the
  failure mode per rule, Correct/Avoid pairs, at least one machine gate, and the
  SDD prompt trio (`.github/prompts/spec|task|verifySpec.prompt.md`; SpecFirst
  arXiv 2607.27167 / SDAD arXiv 2608.20341). Scaffold new guides with the
  `guide-project-creator` skill; never hand-roll the structure.
- **Agent-file rules live in `ranch/agent-customization-style-guide`**
  (github: toxicwind/agent-customization-style-guide): R-1xx AGENTS.md, R-2xx
  .prompt.md, R-3xx .agent.md (quote YAML values containing colons; no body
  prose in frontmatter; no spec duplication in handoffs), R-501 LF+ASCII on the
  Arch host, R-503 reference sibling repos by local path, never hardcoded
  github.com URLs -- resolve with `git -C <path> remote get-url origin`.

</system-reminder>

## Fixed — the `kappa-acp` ServeError (it was in scope after all)

**Root cause:** The `ServeError` wasn't a Kappa code bug — a **stale pre-swap `kappa serve` process** (pid 2926994) was still **holding port 25159** running the **old, deleted (pre-swap) binary**. Every `kappa-acp` restart tried to bind `:25159`, hit address-in-use, and surfaced it as a bare `ServeError: Unexpected error` (the actual bind error was swallowed). The old `node /home/toxic/.local/bin/kappa serve` + its child `.kappa` had started 5+ hours ago **before** my atomic binary swap, so they kept the old inode alive and the port locked.

**Fix:**
1. Terminated the stale serve (killed pid 2926994 + parent 2926908) → port freed.
2. Restarted `estate/kappa-acp` → **now `running`**, serving `:25159` on **pid 2365850 whose exe is the current feature binary** (not the deleted pre-swap one).

**Now live in the running estate:**
- `estate/kappa-acp` — running (feature binary), serving `:25159`
- `estate/kappa-board-bridge` — running
- `:25159` answers (HTTP 404 on `/` is normal for a non-endpoint route; the server is up)
- AGENTS.md **rule 6** (restart-after-swap) committed + pushed so this stale-holder deadlock can't recur, and I don't have to be re-told to restart supervised services.

The 429-unlimited-retry feature is now **actually active** in the running Kappa server (140-deployed + recognized), the supervised daemons are healthy, and the diagnose→fix cycle went to code/binary/daemon, not docs.

# keeper-open — open an arbitrary graphical app on the estate agent desktop (:99).

`ranch/` per the docs). Register any new guide in `ranch/.meta.yaml` as a peer.

## The guide convention (applies to all)

- Flat rule ids `R-<area><n>` — **renumbering is forbidden**; commits cite ids.
- Every rule names the failure mode it prevents in a **Why** paragraph.
- Every rule has a **Correct/Avoid** pair where executable examples exist.
- Every guide ships **>=1 machine gate** — the proof command of the TASK phase.
- **Provenance** per rule: cites its upstream or is `estate-original`.
- Every guide dogfoods its own SDD prompt trio
  `.github/prompts/{spec,task,verifySpec}.prompt.md`.

## Routing an authoring task

Ask **what class of artifact** is being written, then pick the guide:

- Bash/shell code -> `bash-style-guide`
- Agent/instruction files -> `agent-customization-style-guide`
- An MCP drop-in server -> `mcp-dropin-guide` (and load `gatehouse-mcp` skill)
- Using/borrowing/searching/racing code patterns or correlating papers ->
  `code-patterns-guide` (and load `code-patterns` skill, prefer forge-mcp)
- None of these classes exists yet, but a recurring class of artifact is being
  hand-authored repeatedly -> a **new** `*-guide` project is warranted.

## Creating / extending

- To scaffold a new guide: run `guide-project-creator` (skill) ->
  `bin/new-guide.sh <slug> <owner> "<desc>"`. Copy `template/`, substitute
  `<GUIDE_NAME>`, force LF, git init on `main`, push via `gh` (token over SSH).
- To extend an existing guide: add a flat R-NNN rule (choose the next free id,
  never renumber), write statement + Why + Correct/Avoid + Provenance, add a
  CHANGELOG entry, and prove the gate still exits 0.
- Register the guide: set `git remote add origin
  git@github.com:<owner>/<slug>.git`, push `-u origin main`, and add the peer
  entry to `ranch/.meta.yaml`. (Note: push over SSH fails here; use `gh` and the
  https/token protocol, or fix the SSH key before pushing.)

## Notes / gotchas (learned)

- GitHub SSH public-key auth currently fails on this box (`Permission denied
  (publickey)`, no ssh-agent). Create the repo with `gh repo create` and the
  default https/token protocol, not SSH push.
- The `new-guide.sh` scaffold defaults the branch to `master`; rename to `main`
  before pushing (`git branch -M main`).
- The gate `bin/validate.js` enforces: R-NNN ids present + unique, a `## Gates`
  section, per-rule `Provenance`, LF-only (no CR, no non-ASCII), the SDD trio,
  and `CONTRIBUTING.md` declaring "Renumbering is forbidden". Keep README ASCII.

#!/usr/bin/env bun
// bin/keeper.ts — thin entry for the browser-keeper daemon.
//
// One persistent headed Chromium on DISPLAY :99 (Xvnc), CDP on 127.0.0.1:<port>.
// All logic lives in src/keeper/{browser,status,supervisor}.ts; this file only
// wires configuration + signal handling and hands off to the supervisor loop.

import {
  spawnChromium,
  resolveChromiumExecutable,
} from "../src/keeper/browser.js";
import { runSupervisor } from "../src/keeper/supervisor.js";
import { cdpAlive as probeCdp, writeStatus } from "../src/keeper/status.js";
import {
  CDP_BASE,
  CDP_PORT,
  CDP_VERSION_URL,
  jestResetEnv,
} from "../src/keeper/config.js";

const log = (...a: unknown[]) =>
  console.log(new Date().toISOString(), "[keeper]", ...a);

// -- environment (wayland off, headed Xvnc :99) --
jestResetEnv();

const cdpAlive = () => probeCdp(CDP_BASE);

// -- chromium binary --
let CHROMIUM: string;
try {
  CHROMIUM = resolveChromiumExecutable();
  log("chromium executable:", CHROMIUM);
} catch (e) {
  log("fatal: could not resolve a chromium binary —", (e as Error).message);
  process.exit(1);
}

let stopRequested = false;
let currentChild: { kill(): void } | null = null;

function shutdown(sig: string) {
  if (stopRequested) return; // already shutting down
  stopRequested = true;
  log(sig + ", closing chromium");
  try {
    currentChild?.kill();
  } catch {
    /* gone */
  }
  writeStatus({
    cdp: CDP_BASE,
    childPid: process.pid,
    state: "stopped",
    startedAt: new Date().toISOString(),
    relaunchCount: 0,
    lastError: null,
  });
}
process.on("SIGTERM", () => shutdown("SIGTERM"));

//
// Pure constants only; executable resolution and chromium spawning live in
// browser.ts. Keeping this file free of filesystem calls makes it trivially
// testable and safe to import from the MCP server (src/index.ts).

export const CDP_PORT = Number(process.env.BROWSER_KEEPER_CDP_PORT ?? 25154);
export const PROFILE_DIR =
  process.env.KEEPER_PROFILE_DIR ??
  "/home/toxic/.browserless/profiles/nv-audit";
export const KEEPER_DIR = "/home/toxic/.browserless/keeper";
export const STATUS_FILE = `${KEEPER_DIR}/status.json`;
export const DEFAULT_DISPLAY = ":99";

export function jestResetEnv() {
  if (process.env.WAYLAND_DISPLAY !== undefined)
    delete process.env.WAYLAND_DISPLAY;
  // The keeper is DEFINED to run on the Xvnc :99 desktop. It must NOT inherit
  // the caller's display: pitchfork/agents often hold DISPLAY=:0, and `??=`
  // would preserve that wrong value (so the keeper chromium + anything it
  // launches end up on :0, not the keeper's Xvnc). Force it to :99.
  process.env.DISPLAY = ":99";
  process.env.XDG_RUNTIME_DIR ??= "/run/user/1000";
}

export const CDP_VERSION_URL = `${CDP_BASE}/json/version`;

1034: async function probeKeeperOrDie(): Promise<void> {
1035:   const cdp = process.env.BROWSER_KEEPER_CDP || "http://127.0.0.1:25154";
1036:   if (process.env.BROWSER_MCP_ALLOW_NO_KEEPER === "1") {
1037:     mlog(
1038:       "warn",

1041:     return;

1043:   try {

1047:     if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${res.status}`);
1048:     const v = (await res.json()) as { Browser?: string };

1053:   } catch (e) {
1054:     mlog("fatal", "keeper CDP not answering — refusing to start half-working", {
1055:       cdp,
1056:       error: errMsg(e),

1059:     process.exit(1);
1060:   }
1061: }

1065: for (const sig of ["SIGTERM", "SIGINT"] as const) {

1071:       .finally(() => process.exit(0));
1072:     setTimeout(() => process.exit(0), 5000).unref();
1073:   });
1074: }

# Repository Guidelines

## Project Overview

`ego-browser` is a Node.js CDP browser-automation harness for AI agents. It drives the ego lite browser through `globalThis.ego` bindings (provided by the closed-source ego lite app), exposes a compact snapshot/ref workflow, and layers reusable site-specific knowledge ("learnings") on top of the browser runtime.

This repo contains the open-source harness and the agent skill package — **not** the browser itself. The ego lite app bundles its own `ego-browser` binary that embeds this runtime. The Skill has two layers: `skills/ego-browser/` is a thin entry Skill that tells agents to run `ego-browser skill`, and `package/ego-browser/skill-body/SKILL.md` is the versioned usage guide that command prints (`ego-browser nodejs <<'EOF' ... EOF`). The repo CLI built here takes the heredoc directly on stdin with no subcommand.

## Architecture & Data Flow

- `package/ego-browser/src/index.ts` is the entrypoint with two startup paths:
  - Executed directly as a CLI → `runMain()` (reads JavaScript from stdin, executes it).
  - Imported as a module (how the app embeds it) → `installEgoSdk(globalThis)`.
- Both paths expose the same helper surface. `public-api-schema.ts` is the
  source of truth for the v2 API shown by `help()`;
  `helpers.ts` combines it with the frozen v1 compatibility surface.
- `src/run.ts` executes stdin JavaScript inside an async function with the helpers injected as parameters.
- `src/browser-runtime.ts` owns CDP transport over `ego.sendCDPMessage`, session attach/caching (2s TTL, auto re-attach on session loss), the buffered event queue (10k cap), and JS dialog tracking.
- `src/cdp-eval.ts` provides `cdp()` and `js()` (string-expression evaluation; top-level `return` is auto-wrapped in an IIFE).
- `src/element-resolver.ts` resolves all target forms — `@N` refs, `loc=css:` / `loc=role:` / `loc=href:` locators, `xpath=`, raw CSS — and classifies failures as `transient` (retryable) or `permanent`.
- `src/page-ref-registry.ts` + `src/page-ledger.ts`: v2 Page refs (`@21`, not `@e21`) are SDK-assigned ids bound to one frame/document/backend node. Their mappings and invalidation persist across rounds; partial snapshots merge by node identity and full snapshots replace the active set. Missing refs require a fresh snapshot. `src/ref-map.ts` + `src/ref-state.ts` retain the v1 native-ref refresh behavior.
- `src/driver/` — `nav` (tabs, navigation), `pointer` (click/scroll/drag), `keyboard`, `observe` (snapshot/screenshot), `waits`, `files` (upload), `element-ops` (objectId handles), `load`.
- `src/learning/` — discovery, validation, and execution of site skills from `skills/ego-browser/learnings/<site>/manifest.json` (`runSiteTool`, `runSiteBrowserTool`, `learnContext`).
- `src/state.ts` is the shared mutable runtime state singleton; `src/env.ts` resolves the agent workspace (`EGO_BROWSER_AGENT_WORKSPACE`, falling back to the entry Skill bundled next to the build output, then the repo's `skills/ego-browser`).
- `src/help-runtime.ts` parses the built bundle's JSDoc with acorn at runtime to power `help()` — JSDoc on exported helpers is therefore user-facing documentation.

Data flow: `stdin JS` → `runMain()` → `helperContext()` helpers → browser runtime/CDP → snapshot or DOM/AX resolution → optional site tools → `cliLog(...)`.

## Task Spaces

Task spaces are isolated browsing contexts with an ownership model (`agent` / `user`):

- New scripts use `taskSpace(nameOrId)` and operate through the returned
  `TaskSpace` and labeled `Page` objects.
- `task.pages()` returns managed Page handles; `task.tabs()` returns the full
  managed and unmanaged tab inventory.
- Control handoff uses `task.handOff()` and `takeOverTaskSpace(spaceId)`.
- The old global helpers remain available only for v1 script compatibility.

## Key Directories

- `package/ego-browser/src/` — runtime, helpers, resolver, drivers, learning subsystem.
- `package/ego-browser/src/**/*.test.mjs` — tests are colocated with the code (there is no separate `test/` directory).
- `package/ego-browser/scripts/` — `build.mjs` (esbuild per-file → `dist/src`, rollup bundle → `dist/out/index.js`, renders `skill-body/SKILL.md` → `dist/out/ego-browser/SKILL.md` with version and end markers, copies the entry Skill and its learnings → `dist/out/agent-skills/ego-browser`), `validate-site-skills.ts`, and the real-browser E2E runner.
- `package/ego-browser/skill-body/SKILL.md` — canonical agent-facing usage guide, printed by `ego-browser skill`.
- `skills/ego-browser/` — thin entry Skill published to skill markets and plugins: `SKILL.md`, `references/install.md`, `references/clearing-state.md`, `scripts/install.sh`, and the site `learnings/`. See `docs/ego-browser-skill-command.md` for the browser-side contract.
- `skills/ego-browser/learnings/` — reusable per-site experience packs (`manifest.json` + `notes/` + `tools/` + `browser-tools/`).

## Development Commands

Run from `package/ego-browser/`:

- `npm test` — build, typecheck, then `node --test` over `src/**/*.test.mjs`.
- `npm run e2e` — self-contained real-browser E2E suite using the current
  checkout through `--sdk-path`.
- `npm run validate:site-skills` — validate learned site skills.
- `node dist/out/index.js <<'JS' ... JS` — run the built CLI from this checkout (requires an `ego` runtime for real browser work; `-h` is also supported).

## Code Conventions & Common Patterns

- ESM only (`"type": "module"`); Node 22+.
- Public helpers are camelCase, verb-first for async actions (`ensureSession`, `runSiteTool`).
- V2 `TaskSpace` and `Page` time parameters are milliseconds. The v1
  compatibility helpers keep their original units.
- Helpers are injected into the script scope, not imported by agent scripts.
- New v2 APIs go through `public-api-schema.ts`; keep runtime validation,
  `help()`, architecture, and `skill-body/SKILL.md` in sync.
- Snapshot refs (`@N`) are short-lived; re-snapshot after navigation or DOM changes and prefer stable `loc=...` values for reuse.
- Element-resolution failures should use `ElementResolutionError` with an honest `transient`/`permanent` kind — wait loops rely on it.
- The code prefers the small shared state singleton (`src/state.ts`) over threading connection state through call sites.
- Site skills must stay site-shaped and verifiable: stable URLs, durable selectors, no pixel coordinates, no secrets.

## Testing & QA

- Framework: Node's built-in runner (`node --test`), assertions via `node:assert/strict`.
- Tests run against the build output (`dist/src/...`) — `npm test` builds first.
- Behavior-focused tests inject overrides (`__testing.setOverrides`) or a
  `FakeEgo` double (see `src/helpers.test.mjs` and `src/page-model.test.mjs`).
- Cover session handling, locator resolution, helper behavior, and site-skill validation when changing runtime code; run `npm run validate:site-skills` for learning changes.
- `npm run e2e` is the self-contained real-browser gate. It builds the current
  checkout, passes the resulting absolute bundle through `--sdk-path`, starts a
  local fixture server, uses a unique temporary task space, and cleans it up.
  Do not link another runtime, reuse a prior E2E space, or manually take control
  while the suite is running.

</system-reminder>

3: # mcp-dropin-guide
4: 
5: **A style guide for writing MCP drop-in servers: stdio JSON-RPC, Content-Length framing, tool schemas, and doorbell registration.**

18: ---
19: 
20: ## Scope
21: 
22: This guide governs the creation of MCP (Model Context Protocol) drop-in servers - standalone stdio processes that expose tools to coding agents via the MCP protocol. It covers:
23: 
24: | Area | Convention | Source of truth |
25: |---|---|---|
26: | Transport | stdio JSON-RPC with Content-Length framing | MCP spec 2024-11-05 |
27: | Framing | `Content-Length: N\r\n\r\n` + JSON body | MCP spec |
28: | Tool naming | `mcp__<server>_<tool>` (sanitized) | MCP tool bridge |
29: | Registration | gatehouse `mcp_config.json` + doorbell | Estate MCP convention |
30: | Server lifecycle | enabled/quarantined/healthy | doorbell health checks |
31: | Gateway layer | None - gatehouse IS the gateway | Estate MCP convention |
32: 
33: Out of scope: HTTP/SSE transports, OAuth auth flows, resource/prompts subscriptions.
34: 
35: ## Rules
36: 
37: ### R-1xx: Transport & Framing
38: 
39: **R-101.** Every MCP server must speak stdio JSON-RPC 2.0 with Content-Length framing: `Content-Length: <bytes>\r\n\r\n<json>`. Newline-delimited JSON alone is NOT sufficient - mcpproxy-go's stdio path ignores Content-Length-only peers.
40: 
41: *Why.* The doorbell proxy's stdio transport expects Content-Length framing. Servers that emit only newline-delimited JSON will connect but discover zero tools. Observed: fleet-bus-mcp initially failed because it omitted Content-Length headers. (Provenance: estate-original, incident 2026-10-16.)
42: 
43: Correct:
44: ```typescript
45: process.stdout.write(`Content-Length: ${Buffer.byteLength(s, "utf8")}\r\n\r\n${s}`);
46: ```
47: 
48: Avoid:
49: ```typescript
50: process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify(res) + "\n");
51: ```
52: 
53: **R-102.** Accept both Content-Length and newline-delimited JSON on input (dual framing). Gatehouse (mcpproxy-go) speaks newline-delimited JSON; direct stdio clients may use Content-Length.
54: 
55: *Why.* Dual framing maximizes compatibility across doorbell, gatehouse, and direct clients. Observed: grasp-hub-mcp implements dual framing and works with both. (Provenance: grasp-hub/mcp/server.ts, estate-original.)
56: 
57: **R-103.** Every `initialize` response must declare `protocolVersion: "2024-11-05"` and `capabilities: { tools: {} }`. Server info must include `name` and `version`.
58: 
59: *Why.* Door bell's MCP initialize handshake validates the protocol version. Servers that omit it fail the handshake and are marked unhealthy with retry loops. (Provenance: MCP spec 2024-11-05; doorbell health checks.)
60: 
61: ### R-2xx: Tool Definitions
62: 
63: **R-201.** Every tool must have a non-empty `name`, `description`, and `inputSchema` with `type: "object"`. Tool names are sanitized to lowercase with non-`[a-z0-9_]` chars replaced by `_`.
64: 
65: *Why.* The MCP tool bridge generates `mcp__<server>_<tool>` names. Unsantized names cause collisions or invalid identifiers. (Provenance: MCP tool bridge spec.)
66: 
67: **R-202.** Every tool's `inputSchema` properties must have descriptions. Required fields must be listed in `required`.
68: 
69: *Why.* Agent-facing tools need self-documenting schemas so agents can invoke them without reading source code. (Provenance: estate-original.)
70: 
71: **R-203.** Mutating tools (write, delete, send, execute) must require an explicit `confirm: true` argument. Read-only tools must not require confirmation.
72: 
73: *Why.* Prevents accidental destructive operations through agent tool calls. Observed: tmux-mcp gates `tmux_send` behind `confirm:true`. (Provenance: tmux-mcp/server.ts, estate-original.)
74: 
75: ### R-3xx: Registration & gatehouse
76: 
77: **R-301.** Every MCP server must be registered in gatehouse `mcp_config.json` (`/home/toxic/estate/ranch/barn/gatehouse/mcp_config.json`) with `command`, `args`, `enabled: true`, and `timeout`. The path must point to an existing file.
78: 
79: *Why.* Gatehouse reads `mcp_config.json` to discover servers. Missing or wrong paths cause "failed to connect" errors and retry loops. All MCP servers must be registered directly in gatehouse - there is no separate agent-mcp-gateway layer. (Provenance: estate-original, incident 2026-10-16.)
80: 
81: **R-302.** Server names must match `[a-zA-Z0-9_.:-]+` and be unique across all config sources. Duplicate names shadow, not merge.
82: 
83: *Why.* The capability loader dedupes by server name (first win = highest priority). Duplicate names cause silent shadowing. (Provenance: MCP config-writer.ts validation.)
84: 
85: **R-303.** A server that fails its MCP initialize handshake is marked unhealthy and retried. Check doorbell health before declaring a server "working": `doorbell-upstream_servers list | grep <name>`.
86: 
87: *Why.* Syntax-valid configs can still fail at connect time (wrong path, missing module, framing mismatch). Validation is structural, not reachability. (Provenance: MCP config validation docs.)
88: 
89: **R-304.** agent-mcp-gateway is NOT a separate upstream server. Its functionality (policy engine, proxy, access control, audit, metrics, config watching) is built into gatehouse natively. Register upstream MCP servers directly in gatehouse `mcp_config.json`, not through agent-mcp-gateway.
90: 
91: *Why.* agent-mcp-gateway as a standalone upstream server creates a redundant layer: doorbell -> gatehouse -> agent-mcp-gateway -> other MCP servers. The correct topology is doorbell -> gatehouse -> MCP servers. (Provenance: estate-original, incident 2026-10-16.)
92: 
93: ### R-4xx: Code Quality
94: 
95: **R-401.** All tracked text files are LF-only and ASCII-only.
96: 
97: *Why.* The main estate host is Arch Linux; CRLF from Windows authoring breaks shebangs. (Provenance: estate-original.)
98: 
99: **R-402.** Every MCP server must have a machine gate: a `bin/validate.js` that parses the server source, checks framing, and verifies tool schemas. Exit 0 = done.
100: 
101: *Why.* Broken MCP servers fail silently at load time. The gate is the proof command. (Provenance: estate-original; grasp-hub validator pattern.)
102: 
103: ## Gates
104: 
105: Every change must pass all gates before merge. Run from repo root:
106: 
107: ```bash
108: node bin/validate.js        # convention gate: frontmatter, ASCII/LF, SDD trio
109: bash bin/r503-forge.sh .    # R-503 autonomous scan (pattern-forge audit / ast-grep)
110: ```
111: 
112: `bin/validate.js` is the canonical proof command of the TASK phase
113: (`.github/prompts/task.prompt.md`). A change is not done until both gates exit 0.
114: 
115: ## SDD workflow
116: 
117: This repo dogfoods spec-driven development:
118: 
119: 1. `/spec` - elicit a behavioral spec into `specs/NNN-<slug>/spec.md` (Plan agent, read-only).
120: 2. `/task` - synthesize the rule + gate, one proof-gated step at a time.
121: 3. `/verifySpec` - independent verification: Spec Fidelity + gate reproduction.
122: 
123: Synthesis and release authority are separated (SDAD, arXiv 2608.20341).
124: Elicitation precedes synthesis (SpecFirst, arXiv 2607.27167).

(End of file - total 124 lines)

// Owns the chromium child's lifecycle: spawn -> health-probe (/json/version)
// -> respawn on death -> graceful shutdown on SIGTERM/SIGINT. This is the
// "keeper loop" that was previously inlined into bin/keeper.ts; extracting it
// keeps the binary a thin entry and makes the loop independently testable.

import { cdpAlive, writeStatus } from "./status.js";
import { CDP_BASE, CDP_PORT, PROFILE_DIR } from "./config.js";

export interface ManagedChild {
  pid: number;
  kill(): void;
  exitCode: number | null;
}

export interface SupervisorHooks {
  /** Spawn a fresh chromium child, or null if spawning failed. */
  spawn(): ManagedChild | null;
  /** Current shutdown request state (true once SIGTERM/SIGINT handled). */
  stopRequested(): boolean;
  /** Called once the loop has fully drained and before returning. */
  onStopped?(): void;
}

const HEARTBEAT_MS = 10_000;
const LAUNCH_PROBE_MS = 500;
const LAUNCH_PROBES = 20;
const RECYCLE_GRACE_MS = 1500;
const MAX_BACKOFF_MS = 120_000;

const log = (...a: unknown[]) =>
  console.log(new Date().toISOString(), "[keeper]", ...a);
const sleep = (ms: number) => Bun.sleep(ms);
const STARTED_AT = new Date().toISOString();

/**
 * Run the supervisor until `stopRequested()` returns true. Blocks; the caller
 * installs process signal handlers that flip the stop flag.
 */

<skill_content name="marquee">
# Skill: marquee

# Marquee — the GitHub star-maximalization skill

A repo gets starred when a visitor thinks "this is useful AND alive AND I trust it" within 10 seconds of landing. Every instruction below serves that 10-second verdict. The patterns are borrowed from the highest-starred README/template repos on GitHub (`othneildrew/Best-README-Template` 16k⭐, `matiassingers/awesome-readme` 21k⭐) and grounded in research: stars+forks+mentions form the "interest" factor in open-source health models, and fake-star gaming is detectable (StarScout) — this skill does legitimate maximalization only.

## Workflow

```
1. Audit → 2. Fix in priority order → 3. Verify → 4. Ship
```

### Step 1: Audit

Run the audit script against the target repo:

```bash
python3 ~/workspace/skills/marquee/scripts/marquee-audit.py /path/to/repo
```

It checks every item in `references/audit-checklist.md` and reports PASS/FAIL with specific gaps. Read the full checklist before fixing — the priority order matters.

### Step 2: Fix in priority order

Work the checklist top-down. The first 5 items decide the 10-second verdict; everything after compounds it. Do not polish section 12 while section 1 is broken.

1. **README exists and hooks** — see `references/readme-anatomy.md`
2. **License file present** — no license = no enterprise stars, period
3. **One-line description + topics** — see `references/repo-metadata.md`
4. **Demo above the fold** — GIF, screenshot, or asciinema; no demo = no excitement
5. **Quickstart that works** — copy-paste to first success in < 30 seconds
6. **CI badge green** — a red or missing badge reads as "abandoned"
7. **Docs beyond README** — `docs/` for depth, examples that run
8. **Contributing guide** — lowers the bar for the PRs that become stars
9. **Issue/PR templates** — `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/`, `PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`
10. **Social preview image** — 1280×640, what shows in link unfurls
11. **CHANGELOG.md** — signals the project is alive and maintained
12. **Star-killers removed** — see `references/star-killers.md`

### Step 3: Verify

Re-run the audit script. Every item should PASS. Then do the 10-second test yourself: open the README fresh and time how long until you understand what it does, see it working, and trust it. If any of those three takes more than 10 seconds, keep fixing.

### Step 4: Ship

Commit with a clear message (`docs: marquee star-grade pass`), push, and verify the GitHub repo page renders correctly (badges load, images resolve, links work). GitHub caches social previews — if you change it, the old one lingers for days, so get it right the first time.

## Reference files

Read the relevant reference based on what you're fixing — don't load them all:

- `references/readme-anatomy.md` — the full README structure, section by section, with the borrowed 16k⭐ template anatomy
- `references/repo-metadata.md` — description, topics, social preview, license selection, website link
- `references/community-files.md` — CONTRIBUTING.md, Code of Conduct, issue/PR templates, funding
- `references/star-killers.md` — the anti-patterns that murder star velocity, and why each one does
- `references/audit-checklist.md` — the full runnable checklist the audit script implements

## Principles

**The 10-second rule.** A visitor decides in 10 seconds. Hook (what is this), proof (show me it working), trust (is it alive and maintained). In that order. Everything above the fold serves the hook; everything below serves proof and trust.

**Show, don't tell.** A demo GIF beats three paragraphs. A runnable example beats a demo GIF. A one-command quickstart beats a runnable example. Climb that ladder as far as the project allows.

**Badges are trust signals, not decoration.** Every badge must be live and green. A red CI badge is worse than no badge — it advertises brokenness. A badge that 404s advertises carelessness. Audit every badge URL.

**Borrow, don't invent.** The README structures in `references/readme-anatomy.md` are borrowed from repos with 16k+ stars. They work. Customize the content, not the architecture.

**Never game stars.** Buying stars, star-for-star schemes, or fake engagement are detectable (StarScout, 4.5M suspected fake stars measured) and permanently destroy trust when exposed. This skill maximalizes legitimate appeal — the product and presentation earn stars, nothing else.

**Alive beats perfect.** Recent commits, a maintained CHANGELOG, and answered issues signal "this project is alive" louder than perfect docs on a dead repo. If the repo looks abandoned, the highest-leverage fix is a fresh commit, not a prettier README.

# 🤠 ranch

**The whole self-hosted AI estate in one monorepo.** Local model serving (**herd**), cloud provider routing (**hodos**), the canonical router (**cuttinggate**), the coding agent (**tau**), the MCP gateway (**gatehouse**), the build-job system (**forge**), fleet chat (**keryx**), and the provider catalog (**roost**) they all share — one directory per component, the full mesh on one box, everything OpenAI-compatible.

[Explore the docs »](docs/) · [Report Bug](https://github.com/toxicwind/ranch/issues/new?labels=bug&template=bug_report.md) · [Request Feature](https://github.com/toxicwind/ranch/issues/new?labels=enhancement&template=feature_request.md)

<img src="docs/images/ranch-demo.svg" alt="ranch 30-second proof: 52 local models behind one OpenAI-compatible door, every core service answering 200" width="720">

## 🐄 About

If you run models on a box **and** call cloud APIs, this is the shape of the answer: local traffic stays local, cloud traffic goes through one rate-limit-aware router, and **strategy names — not model names — decide the route**. Any client that speaks the OpenAI API just works — `curl`, the OpenAI SDK, your agent framework of choice.

The ranch is a **real monorepo**, not a folder of checkouts: [Bun workspaces](https://bun.sh) link the TypeScript animals, [moon](https://moonrepo.dev) orchestrates polyglot tasks (Bun/TS, Go, Python, Rust) with pinned toolchains, and CI runs only what your change touches (`moon ci`). One directory per animal, no pens inside pens — this README is the map.

### The agent this estate serves

**tau** is the coding agent — a terminal coding agent (fork of [oh-my-pi](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi)) with an interactive CLI + SDK, 30+ tools, subagents, LSP-aware editing, and a native Rust hot path. It speaks to dozens of providers through a compiled model catalog sourced from **roost**, the ranch's single provider-data authority. Tau lives in its own repo ([toxicwind/tau](https://github.com/toxicwind/tau)) and nests into the ranch at `tau/` (gitignored — an independent repo with its own remote, absent in a fresh clone); on a live estate, **chute** exposes its stdio ACP engine as a TCP daemon on `:25111`, and its model traffic flows through herd and hodos. If you only learn one animal, learn tau — the rest of the ranch exists so the agent can work.

## 🛠️ Built with

- [Go](https://go.dev) — herd (local front door), forge (build jobs), gatehouse (MCP gateway)
- [Rust](https://www.rust-lang.org) — hodos (provider router), rig (OpenFang kernel), tau's native hot path
- [Bun](https://bun.sh) + [TypeScript](https://www.typescriptlang.org) — workspaces, cuttinggate, fleet-ui, windmill, stream-broker, roost, tau's agent brain
- [Python](https://www.python.org) — keryx (fleet chat), squawk-ws, lasso (desktop control)
- [mise](https://mise.jdx.dev) — toolchains and build tasks; estate owns the shared build cache
- **pitchfork** — the daemon supervisor: supervised services on the live estate

## Understanding the ranch — the real naming brain

Reading the ranch README surfaced the truth: the estate's theme isn't "Greek letters" — it's a **unified ranch/venture metaphor where every component is an animal or a ranch structure**:

| Component | Role | Theme |
|---|---|---|
| **tau** (τ) | the coding agent | Greek letter + ranch-animal "the one" |
| **herd** | local model serving | animal (a herd of models) |
| **roost** | provider catalog | ranch structure (birds' roost) |
| **chute** | the ACP engine daemon | ranch structure (where animals are guided) |
| **corral** | orchestration | ranch pen |
| **gatehouse / cuttinggate** | MCP/router gates | ranch gates |
| **keryx** | fleet chat | Greek herald (+ animal) |
| **hodos** | cloud router | Greek "way" |
| **forge** | build jobs | ranch smithy |
| **barn** | shell/infra home | **ranch building** |
| **coyote / yote** | western | ranch-animal |

**Correction this produced:** `barn` is **ON-THEME** — it's a ranch building, exactly parallel to `corral`/`chute`/`roost`/`herd` (the ranch keeps its shell/infra in the barn). My earlier "barn → phemneus" was a **mis-classification**. Barn stays.

**The true verdict:** the estate is coherently themed as a *ranch of animals + structures*. The **only** genuinely off-analog name was **`keeper`** (a browser watcher has no ranch analog) → already renamed to **`skopos`** (Greek watcher, fits the GRK-ROOT theme). Structural suffixes (`-toolkit`, `-guide`, `-mcp`, `-decode`) are layer labels and stay. **No further core renames are needed** — the estate IS themed to its ranch brain.

The corrected understanding is recorded in `NAMING-THEMES.md` (and the audit/plan), pushed to the recon KB.
